<!-- agent-pr-review:readiness round=1 -->
## Readiness review (round 1): Needs answers

**Issue:** #236 [M3] Offer format: grouped by day, five options in total across days, spread over broad requests, patient on repeats (#212) · **Read at:** 2026-10-15 18:07 UTC · **Default branch:** `main` @ `c05cb79`

The issue asks for four things. The first is one offer format in the system prompt: times grouped under a day line, five options in total across all days (#212). The second is a rule for spreading options over a broad request. The third is a plain answer when a patient repeats a question. The fourth is grader support and eval cases for all of it. The most important point to settle is how a broad request gets spread at all (Q-1), because `check_availability` only ever returns the earliest five slots. Next is the exact format and how the weekday/ET check reads a time under a day line (Q-2). The work can't start until #239's grader PR is on `main`.

Round: 1 · Questions: 4 · Assumptions: 8 · Suggested edits: 10 · Spec commit: c05cb79c1aaa1b7d3c0c4281ec17a1b1777a261d · Harness version: 2026.10.11.1

**Check these first:** A-2, A-4, A-6

**To answer:** reply on this issue with one line per item, in the form shown under each (`Decision r1/<ID>: <answer>`): an option's letter or your own words for a question, "accept" or "reject" for an edit, "ok" or your correction for an assumption. To take every recommendation and edit at once, `Decision r1/ALL: accept`; it does not cover the assumptions under "Check these first" or those marked "(verify first)" or "(would have asked)", which each need their own line. Only `Decision` lines are applied, never other replies. Then ask for the apply step, which writes your answers into the issue's description.

### Questions

#### Q-1: When a patient asks about a whole week or longer ("next week", "any time"), how does the agent spread its five options across days?

- **Why it matters:** One search can't spread. `check_availability` returns only the earliest five matches and walks the days in order (`packages/tools/src/tools/check_availability.ts:8-9`, `:168-171`), and its input has no spread option (`packages/contracts/src/tools.ts:118-129`). So one search over "next week" returns Monday's first slots, which is exactly what Nick saw. Each way of spreading changes three things: the tool calls the agent makes, the time to first text (already over NFR-001's 3 s p50 at 4,735 ms, #251), and two smoke L1 cases in the Eval gate's baseline. A wrong guess means rewriting the prompt rule and its eval cases.
- **Source:** AC 2: "The exact rule is settled in this issue's readiness review, and stays within the five-option limit". PRD §5 rule 2: "Offer concrete options, not open questions, when possible" (`docs/PRD.md:110`). `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:119`: "Prefer concrete options to open questions." `system.v3.ts:131`: "(the earliest first when nothing narrows it down)".
- **Options:** (one per line)
  - (a) Search each day in the same reply. Once the kind of visit or the provider is known, and the request covers more than one weekday with no specific time, the agent makes one `check_availability` call per weekday, all in the same reply, for at most the first five weekdays of the range. It keeps any time of day the patient gave. It then offers up to five options: at most two per day, days in date order, earliest first within a day. A day with fewer slots leaves its share to the following days. Time to first text adds no model call, because the loop runs one reply's calls together (`packages/agent/src/loop.ts:362-376`) and allows 16 calls per turn (`loop.ts:71`). It costs up to five tool results instead of one. The smoke L1 cases `l1-availability-specialty-next-week` and `l1-availability-after-dst` expect one whole-week search. Each case's `end_date` list therefore gains the range's first day, so that the Monday-only search matches. A case passes when any call matches (`packages/evals/src/graders/matchers.ts:44-47`). Scope: within the issue
  - (b) Search the whole range, then widen if it bunches. The agent searches the whole range once. If every slot returned falls on one day and `truncated` is true, it searches again in the same turn, from the next day to the end of the range. It then offers up to five over the days found: at most two per day, days in date order. The first call is unchanged, so no L1 case changes. A result that bunches, which is the usual case for a week, adds one model call before the first text. Scope: within the issue
  - (c) Ask first when nothing narrows the request. If the request names neither a day nor a time of day, the agent asks one question first: a preferred day, or morning or afternoon. If it names either, the agent searches the whole range once and offers the earliest five, grouped by day. Nothing is spread, so "next week, afternoons" still gets one day's times. This departs from PRD §5 rule 2, and `system.v3.ts:119` must be reworded. Scope: within the issue
  - (d) Spread inside the tool. `check_availability` gains a per-day cap or a spread input, so one call returns slots across days. This is a cross-stream contract change on a gated path, and it re-pins the contract snapshot (`packages/contracts/src/tools.test.ts:68`). Scope: adds a tool and contract change. Owned paths: + `packages/tools/src/tools/check_availability.ts`, + `packages/tools/test/tools/check_availability.test.ts`, + `packages/contracts/src/tools.test.ts` and its snapshot under `packages/contracts/src/__snapshots__/`
- **Makes stale:** by option, one line each:
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:131` ("the earliest first when nothing narrows it down"): all options
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.test.ts:273-278` (the #171 guard quotes that sentence): all options
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/l1/l1-availability-specialty-next-week.yaml:18`: option (a)
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/l1/l1-availability-after-dst.yaml:19`, `:27`: option (a)
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:119`: option (c)
  - `packages/tools/src/tools/check_availability.ts:8-9`, `packages/contracts/src/tools.ts:237`: option (d)
- **Edges:** each case below is settled by the choice.
  - **Broad requests:** a range of two or more weekdays with no specific time, with or without a time of day. "Next week, afternoons" is broad (under (a), one afternoon search per day).
  - **Not broad:**
    - One named day.
    - "The earliest" or "soonest you have": one search, earliest first.
    - A specific time over a range ("11:30, any day that week"). This keeps the #170 rule: one search over the range with `start_time` (`system.v3.ts:132`), so `l1-availability-specific-later-time` stays as is.
    - "This week" with one weekday left: one day.
  - **More than five weekdays** ("the next two weeks", "October"): only the first five weekdays are searched, and the reply says later times exist.
  - **Fewer than five open slots in total:** all are offered.
  - **The exact limit:** five open days give 2+2+1 (the first three days).
  - **Concurrency:** the per-day calls are reads that run together, and a slot taken before booking still gets SLOT_UNAVAILABLE (`system.v3.ts:144`). Nothing new interleaves.
  - **Gate tolerance:** under (a), leaving both smoke L1 cases unchanged would be two L1 regressions, past the one per mode that the Eval gate accepts. Their edits are part of the work, and the PR says so.
  - **Evidence:** the broad-request L1 cases from Q-4, and the gate's L1 run.
- **Recommendation:** (a). It keeps concrete options (PRD §5 rule 2, `docs/PRD.md:110`; `system.v3.ts:119`). It adds no model call before the first text, which #251 shows is already over target. It stays inside the owned paths, where the two case edits live (`packages/evals/scenarios/**`).
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-1: (a)`

#### Q-2: What exactly does a grouped offer look like, and how does the weekday/ET check read a time under a day line?

- **Why it matters:** AC 1 fixes the day line, but not where "ET" and the provider go. Three things in the code depend on that choice:
  - The weekday/ET check wants ET within 16 characters after each time (`packages/evals/src/graders/text.ts:211-226`).
  - The option count treats a time two providers share as two options (r1/A-1, `text.ts:197-198`).
  - Once #239 pairs a listed time with its day line, the second and later times under one day line find no weekday in their 40-character window, because the previous mention is the floor (`text.ts:223-224`). They fail `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` unless this issue changes the check.

  #239 also hands over gate run 4's heading, which this format must handle. Choosing the wrong format means rewriting the prompt, its guards, the grader and the cases.
- **Source:** AC 1: "one plain-text day line per day ("Monday, October 12:") followed by that day's times in ET". AC 4. #239 AC 3: "Its `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` failure is left to #236 (the offer format), not hidden here". ADR-008: "every date + time in assistant text carries a weekday and ET" (`docs/adr/0008-evaluation-strategy.md:128`). FR-030: "with provider and weekday" (`docs/PRD.md:83`).
- **Options:** (one per line)
  - (a) ET after every time, and the provider on each line only when there are several providers. Scope: within the issue
    - **Day line:** only the weekday, the date and a colon ("Tuesday, October 13:"), with no time and no other words.
    - **Time lines:** each time is its own "- " line with ET after it.
    - **Provider:** when the offer has more than one provider, each time line names one ("- 1:00 PM ET with Dr. Priya Lee"); otherwise the provider is named once in the lead-in ("Dr. Lee has these openings:"). A time two providers share is two lines.
    - **Grader:** `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` takes a listed time's weekday from the nearest day line above it, and looks for ET on the time's own line. A time written inside a day line or in prose keeps today's rule, so gate run 4's heading still fails. `max_five_options` is unchanged.
    - **Docs:** ADR-008's line stays true, because each listed time still has a weekday and ET. The scenarios README's row is reworded.
  - (b) ET and the provider on every time line. Scope: within the issue
    - **Day line:** only the weekday, the date and a colon ("Tuesday, October 13:"), with no time and no other words.
    - **Time lines:** each time is its own "- " line with ET after it and its provider, even when the offer has only one provider ("- 8:00 AM ET with Dr. Lee"). A time two providers share is two lines. Replies are longer, and FR-030's "with provider" holds for each option on its own.
    - **Grader:** `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` takes a listed time's weekday from the nearest day line above it, and looks for ET on the time's own line. A time written inside a day line or in prose keeps today's rule, so gate run 4's heading still fails. `max_five_options` is unchanged.
    - **Docs:** ADR-008 `:128` stays true. The scenarios README's row is reworded.
  - (c) ET once, on the day line. The day line is "Tuesday, October 13 (ET):" and the times under it are bare ("- 1:00 PM with Dr. Priya Lee"). `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` takes both the weekday and the zone from the day line. That changes what ADR-008 `:128` says, so it needs a dated amendment. Scope: adds an ADR-008 amendment. Owned paths: + `docs/adr/0008-evaluation-strategy.md`, + `docs/adr/README.md`
- **Makes stale:** by option, one line each:
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:126` (the per-time "weekday and date" example): all options
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:131` ("each with the weekday, date, time in ET, and provider name"): all options
  - `packages/evals/src/graders/text.ts:213-217` (the `mentionHasWeekdayAndZone` doc): all options
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/README.md:117`: all options
  - `docs/adr/0008-evaluation-strategy.md:128`: option (c) only
- **Edges:** each case below is settled by the choice.
  - **Accepted:** "Tuesday, October 13:\n- 1:00 PM ET with Dr. Priya Lee" passes.
  - **Rejected under (a) and (b):** "Tuesday, October 13:\n- 1:00 PM with Dr. Priya Lee" fails (no ET).
  - **Rejected under every option:** "Tuesday, October 13 (earlier than your 2:30 PM visit):" fails (a time inside a day line, no ET). The prompt keeps `system.v3.ts:133`, "mention that time without its date".
  - **Single-day offer:** it still has one day line.
  - **A listed time with no day line above it and no date on its line:** no date-time mention, so it isn't graded, as today.
  - **A merged "Dr. Lee or Dr. Okafor" line:** the prompt doesn't allow it, and it would count as one option (`text.ts:201-208`).
  - **Which pairing:** #239's (A-6), not a second parser.
  - **Scope:** the restatement and the confirmation are outside the format (A-3).
  - **Evidence:** grader tests in `packages/evals/test/` on hand-built grouped messages, each seen failing with `npm run mutate`.
- **Recommendation:** (a). It keeps ET where the grader already looks (`text.ts:211-226`) and keeps r1/A-1's counting, with one line per provider and time. It needs no ADR amendment outside the owned paths, and it is the shortest form that still names the provider (FR-030, `docs/PRD.md:83`).
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-2: (a)`

#### Q-3: Is #212's cap (five options in total across all days) held by the prompt's wording alone, or also by a guard in code?

- **Why it matters:** #212 makes this the owner's decision before work starts. A guard is a loop change outside the owned paths. Replies stream to the patient as they are written (`packages/agent/src/loop.ts:339`), so a guard could only discard a streamed reply (`text_reset`, `loop.ts:13`) and retry, which costs a model call on each miss.
- **Source:** the "From #212" criteria: "Either change the "Offering times" wording, or add a guard outside the prompt. Which one is the owner's decision, made on this issue before work starts." #212's owned paths: "`packages/agent/src/**` and `packages/agent/test/**` (only if a guard outside the prompt is chosen)" (#212 description).
- **Options:** (one per line)
  - (a) Prompt only. The "Offering times" rule says at most five options in one message, counted across all day lines, not five per day, and a content guard pins the sentence. Scope: within the issue
  - (b) Prompt plus a loop guard. The "Offering times" rule says at most five options in one message, counted across all day lines, and a content guard pins the sentence. In addition, the loop counts the options in a final reply; above five, it discards the reply with `text_reset` and retries once with a nudge. The counting rule (`offeredClockTimes`, `packages/evals/src/graders/text.ts:201-208`) moves to a new module that both the agent and the evals import. Each miss costs one extra model call. Scope: adds a loop change. Owned paths: + `packages/agent/src/loop.ts`, + `packages/agent/test/**`, + `packages/contracts/src/offer-count.ts` (new), + `packages/contracts/src/offer-count.test.ts` (new), + `packages/contracts/src/index.ts`
- **Makes stale:** by option, one line each:
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.ts:131`: both options
  - `packages/agent/src/prompts/system.v3.test.ts:273-278`: both options
  - `packages/agent/src/loop.ts:6-20` (header contract): option (b)
- **Edges:** each case below is settled by the choice.
  - **The exact limit:** five listed times across two day lines pass; six fail with "6 times in one message" (`packages/evals/src/graders/invariants.ts:278`).
  - **Shared times:** a time two providers share counts twice (r1/A-1).
  - **Times outside the list:** a time repeated in prose after the list is not an option (`text.ts:192-196`).
  - **Evidence:** the branch reruns of #212's two scenarios, with the over-five count in the PR, and the content guard's KILLED row from `npm run mutate`.
- **Recommendation:** (a). AC 1 rewrites the "Offering times" section anyway. Before this one over-five reply, #171's prompt change held in 8 of 8 trials (#212 description, "History"). A guard would add a model call per miss to a turn that is already over NFR-001's p50 (#251), and it lives outside the owned paths.
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-3: (a)`

#### Q-4: What kind of eval cases does AC 5 add, do they join the smoke suite, and what does each one check?

- **Why it matters:**
  - **Multi-turn scenarios** are pinned at 41 by the lint (`packages/evals/test/scenarios-lint.test.ts:30`, `:57`) and by ADR-008's budget, which only an amendment changes (`docs/adr/0008-evaluation-strategy.md:236-238`, the precedent from #230).
  - **Smoke cases** change the gate's baseline.
  - **L1** runs neither `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` nor `max_five_options` (`packages/evals/src/l1.ts:202-214`), so an L1 case has to carry its own response checks.

  Building the wrong kind of case wastes the case work and its eval spend.
- **Source:** AC 5: "Eval cases: a single-day offer and a multi-day offer in the grouped format, a broad "next week" request that gets spread or a narrowing question, and a repeated question." The issue is silent on mode, smoke and assertions.
- **Options:** (one per line)
  - (a) Five L1 cases, run in the full suite only and not tagged smoke, so the baseline is unchanged. Scope: within the issue
    - **Single-day offer:** a one-day result in the context. The reply must contain "Tuesday, October 13:" and must match none of `October 13[\s\S]*October 13`. That regex rejects "- Tuesday, October 13 at 1:00 PM ET\n- Tuesday, October 13 at 1:30 PM ET" and accepts "Tuesday, October 13:\n- 1:00 PM ET\n- 1:30 PM ET".
    - **Multi-day offer:** results on two days. Both day lines must appear, and each date at most once.
    - **Broad request, next action:** "next week" for a known specialty. Under per-day searches, the expected action is a `check_availability` call whose date range is one later weekday (2026-10-14 to 2026-10-14), which a single whole-week call fails. Under a narrowing question, it is a reply with at most one question.
    - **Broad request, reply:** per-day results for five open days in the context. The reply must contain the day lines of the first three days. Under a narrowing question, this case is dropped.
    - **Repeated question:** an earlier offer in the context and the same question again. The reply must contain the day line again and must contain none of "showed those", "above", "already showed", "as I mentioned".
  - (b) Five L1 cases (single-day offer, multi-day offer, broad request's next action, broad request's reply, repeated question), with the response checks listed under Q-4 (a), and the single-day and multi-day cases tagged smoke. The Eval gate then checks the format on every gated PR, and `packages/evals/baselines/sonnet-4.6.json` gains their ids (owned, "only if a new case joins the smoke set"). Scope: within the issue
  - (c) Multi-turn scenarios for the broad-request and repeated-question cases, which see the whole turn and the scenario-only invariants, with L1 cases for the other two. This needs an ADR-008 budget amendment and new lint pins. Scope: adds an ADR-008 amendment. Owned paths: + `docs/adr/0008-evaluation-strategy.md`, + `docs/adr/README.md`
- **Makes stale:** by option, one line each:
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/README.md:6` ("37 of them"): options (a) and (b)
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/README.md:154` and `:159` (FR-030 and FR-035 coverage rows): all options
  - `packages/evals/scenarios/README.md:5`, `packages/evals/test/scenarios-lint.test.ts:30`, `:57`: option (c)
  - `packages/evals/baselines/sonnet-4.6.json:15-24`: option (b)
- **Edges:** each case below is settled by the choice.
  - **Fixed values:** each case uses the `clinic-default` fixture with the clock at Mon Oct 5, 9:00 AM EDT, and each canned result copies `start_local` from `formatClinicDateTime` (`packages/tools/src/clock.ts:163-168`).
  - **Spending:** the first live run of the new cases is `--suite full --filter <ids>` at `--trials 1`. Its dry-run estimate is stated before it runs.
  - **The case list is a minimum.** The agent may add a case for the merged-provider line.
  - **Evidence:** the results table in the PR, and the scenario lint passing.
- **Recommendation:** (a). It stays inside the owned paths and needs no budget amendment. It also follows the rule #201 sets for new cases ("none is tagged `smoke` unless Nick decides otherwise"). The smoke scenario `book-derm-next-week-afternoon` already grades a grouped offer in scenario mode through `max_five_options` and `times_in_clinic_tz_with_weekday` (`packages/evals/scenarios/book/book-derm-next-week-afternoon.yaml:28-29`).
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-4: (a)`
